description.narrative: TradeMark Africa's Djibouti Country Programme works to strengthen the competitiveness and efficiency of the Djibouti–Ethiopia corridor, one of the region's most strategically significant trade routes, handling over 90% of landlocked Ethiopia's sea-borne trade through Djibouti's ports at the Bab el-Mandeb strait. Operating since 2021, the Programme supports the operationalisation of the Djibouti–Ethiopia–South Sudan–Uganda (DESSU) Corridor Management Authority as a platform for coordinated corridor governance and non-tariff barrier elimination, while advancing digital trade systems including electronic cargo tracking, fleet management, and the integration of customs and port regulatory platforms. Complementary interventions strengthen Djibouti's standards and sanitary and phytosanitary infrastructure through the Djibouti Agency for Standards and Quality (ADN), upgrade physical trade infrastructure at the Galafi border post and PK-51 logistics hub, and promote inclusive economic participation by supporting women- and youth-led enterprises in high-potential sectors such as fisheries and cool logistics.

receiver-org.narrative: TradeMark Africa (TMA) is a leading Aid-for-Trade organisation founded in 2010 to grow intra-African trade, increase Africa’s share in global trade, and make trade more pro-poor and sustainable. We operate on a not-for-profit basis, funded by a strong coalition of development partners including Canada, Denmark, the European Union, Finland, France, the Gates Foundation, Ireland, the Mastercard Foundation, the Netherlands, Norway, Sweden and the United Kingdom. TMA works closely with regional and continental institutions, national governments, the private sector, and civil society to unlock trade and investment opportunities across the continent.
